claim_1.claim: CITE-seq analysis of PBMCs from 7 COVID-19 patients and 5 healthy controls showed an induction of interferon-stimulated genes (IFI27, IFITM3, ISG15) in COVID-19 patients, which was absent in healthy controls.

sources.quote: Notably, we detected clusters of T cells and monocytes that were characterized by the expression of interferon-stimulated genes (ISGs) such as IFI27, IFITM3, or ISG15.

Cryopreserved PBMC samples from a total of 12 age-matched subjects in the Atlanta cohort (five healthy controls and seven COVID-19 patients; Table 2) were enriched for DCs, stained using a cocktail of 36 DNA-labeled antibodies (table S2), and analyzed using droplet-based single-cell gene expression profiling approaches.

claim_2.claim: Bulk RNA-seq analysis of PBMCs from 17 COVID-19 patients and 17 healthy controls showed a strong induction of interferon-stimulated genes in COVID-19 patients compared with healthy controls.

sources.quote: We observed a strong induction of the ISGs in COVID-19 subjects compared with healthy donors in this dataset as well.
We performed bulk RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) analysis of PBMCs in an extended group of subjects (17 COVID-19 patients and 17 healthy controls) from the same cohort.

claim_3.claim: CyTOF analysis of PBMCs from 52 COVID-19 patients and 62 healthy controls showed a significant reduction in the frequency of plasmacytoid dendritic cells in COVID-19 patients compared to healthy controls.

sources.quote: There were several differences, but notably the frequency of plasmacytoid dendritic cells (pDCs) was significantly reduced in the PBMCs of SARS-CoV-2–infected individuals in both cohorts.

We used mass cytometry to assess immune responses to SARS-CoV-2 infection in 52 COVID-19 patients, who were confirmed positive for viral RNA by polymerase chain reaction (PCR), and 62 age- and gender-matched healthy controls distributed between the two cohorts.

claim_4.claim: Flow Cytometry analysis of ex vivo stimulated PBMCs from COVID-19 patients showed reduced production of IFN-α and TNF-α in plasmacytoid dendritic cells compared to healthy controls.

sources.quote: Consistent with our hypothesis, there was reduced production of IFN-α in response to the TLR stimuli in the pDCs of infected individuals compared with those of healthy controls.

claim_5.claim: Olink assay of plasma from COVID-19 patients showed significant up-regulation of cytokines including IL-6, MCP-3, and CXCL10 compared to healthy controls.

sources.quote: Of these 71 proteins, 43 cytokines, including IL-6, MCP-3, and CXCL10, were significantly up-regulated in COVID-19 infection.

claim_6.claim: ELISA validation of plasma from severe and ICU COVID-19 patients confirmed increased levels of inflammatory mediators TNFSF14, EN-RAGE, and OSM compared to healthy controls.

sources.quote: Consistent with the multiplex Olink analysis, we found a significant increase of these inflammatory mediators in the plasma of severe and intensive care unit (ICU) COVID-19 patients.

claim_7.claim: Q-PCR analysis of plasma from severe and ICU COVID-19 patients showed significantly higher levels of bacterial DNA compared to healthy controls.

sources.quote: Notably, the plasma of severe and ICU patients had significantly higher levels of bacterial DNA, as measured by PCR quantitation of bacterial 16 S ribosomal RNA (rRNA) gene product.
